depicted_variant: Lagerlöf joyful Närke wind witch at whirlwind centre with cloud-whirling hair and duststorm skirt
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Square mature painterly mythology encyclopedia artwork. YSÄTTERS-KAJSA / Ysätter-Kaisa, playful Swedish wind witch described by Selma Lagerlöf. One joyful mature human-shaped woman with ordinary coherent human face, human ears and normal hands, smiling mischievously at the CENTRE OF A WHIRLWIND. Her very long dark-grey hair whirls naturally upward among storm clouds, while the hem of her modest plain earth-brown long dress sweeps and trails like a rolling dust storm across empty rural Närke landscape. Garment stays opaque and covers body. Two arms clearly separate from billowing fabric, hands extended in a lively balanced wind stance. Distant Swedish forest and farm fields beneath a strong gale, swirling leaves and dust only as weather. Happy spirited personality, not grim horror. No horns, tail, claws, pointed ears, rocks growing from skin, extra limbs, lightning from hands, disaster victims or text. Elegant detailed atmospheric brushwork with deep forest-green shadows and restrained antique-gold highlights. Main head and hands entirely contained in frame. No signature, border, watermark, gore, nudity or unintended extra anatomy.
visual_requirements: Hair swirling among clouds and skirt sweeping like dust storm
Swedish gale landscape, no invented troll anatomy
aura: Exuberant mischievous wind and vigorous Swedish weather
nonhuman_features: Playful supernatural wind being standing at whirlwind centre with hair in clouds and duststorm skirt; no anatomical deformation claimed
historical_basis: Lagerlöf's literary account of Närke's Ysätter-Kaisa describes her joyful gale-loving nature, hair among clouds and skirt dragging like a duststorm. Physical interpretation retains normal woman-shaped form; does not invent modern troll horns or tails.
artistic_changes: Specific woman face and dress, whirlwind shape, distant farm landscape and illumination are artistic interpretation. Enlarged visual presentation against landscape conveys wind personification and is not asserted as a separate literal giant-height claim.

visual_review.notes: Individually viewed original: one joyful normal woman-shaped wind spirit centred amid swirling clouds and leaves, long hair whirls among clouds, opaque brown skirt trailing like dust storm, two coherent ordinary arms/hands, Swedish fields/forest/farms below. No horns, tail, claws, pointed ears, lightning spell, extra limbs or writing. Large scene scale is expressive storm personification, not new morphology.
